title: With `errorRecovery`, a declaration whose value fails its property's grammar is kept, and no warning is reported
impact: No reactions, no project named; agent-style batch. The reported behavior (keep as written, no warning) is long-standing and deliberate. A related real bug found while checking: for properties in FallbackHandler (color, fill, stroke, filter, backdrop-filter, text-shadow, caret-color, caret) a grammar-failing value REPLACES the earlier valid fallback, e.g. `color:red;color:bananas` -> `color:bananas` (also `color:red;color:contrast-color(red)`), since 1.21.0, in strict and errorRecovery mode. Same root cause as open #1392; that one is medium (fallbacks before newer color functions Lightning CSS does not parse are a realistic pattern).
code: src/properties/mod.rs: Property::parse falls back to Property::Unparsed ('Ideally we'd only do this if var() or env() references were seen, but err on the safe side for now.')
src/properties/prefix_handler.rs: define_fallbacks! Unparsed branch ('Unparsed properties are always "valid"...') — related #1392 bug
summary: A known property whose value fails its grammar becomes Property::Unparsed and is printed as written, in strict mode too, with no warning. This is deliberate: Lightning CSS cannot tell a typo from a value it does not parse yet (new keywords/functions), and keeping it is meaning-preserving because the browser drops it at the same place. It matches the CLAUDE.md errorRecovery contract (recover like a browser, keep CSS as written); only the website docs sentence 'omitting them in the output' (which describes declarations that fail to tokenize/parse at all, e.g. `width: 10px )`, which ARE dropped with a warning) is imprecise. The visitor point (Unparsed for both var() and invalid values) is by design; visitors can inspect the tokens.
repro: 1404-repro.mjs. `.a{width:10px;width:notalength}` -> kept unchanged (correct, control). Related #1392 cases: `.a{color:red;color:bananas}` -> `.a{color:bananas}` (wrong since 1.21.0; 1.20.0 kept both).
evidence: Ran strict and errorRecovery on master: width/display/background-color invalid values kept as written in both modes, no warnings; `width: 10px )` -> dropped with warning 'Unexpected token CloseParenthesis'. repro.mjs --range 1.14.0..1.33.0: controls correct (width case briefly wrong 1.21.0-1.27.0, fixed since 1.28.0); FallbackHandler cases WRONG 1.21.0..master. Chromium equivalence on `.a{color:red;color:bananas}`: input red, output black (NOT EQUIVALENT); width case equivalent.

fix.approach: For #1404 itself: reword the docs sentence (declarations the parser cannot read are dropped with a warning; values Lightning CSS does not recognize are kept as written). Optional enhancement: a warning for an Unparsed value with no var()/env()/attr(). The FallbackHandler bug belongs to #1392: only let an Unparsed value replace the earlier declaration when it contains var()/env() (or other parse-time-valid substitutions), else push it after the earlier one.

subcases.case: FallbackHandler: invalid value replaces earlier valid fallback (color, fill, filter, text-shadow, ...)
subcases.cause: prefix_handler.rs define_fallbacks! Unparsed branch treats every Unparsed as parse-time valid
subcases.status: open, same root cause as #1392 (which reports it for unresolvable relative colors); since 1.21.0

draftReply:
Thanks for the detailed report. Keeping these declarations is intentional: when a value doesn't match a property's grammar, Lightning CSS can't tell a typo from a newer value it doesn't parse yet, so it keeps the declaration as written rather than dropping it, in strict mode too. A browser ignores it at the same point, so the result doesn't change. The docs sentence you quoted is about declarations that can't be parsed at all (e.g. `width: 10px )`), which are dropped with a warning. It should say that more clearly.

While checking this we found a related bug: for `color`, `fill`, `filter`, `text-shadow` and a few others, such a value replaces an earlier valid fallback (`color:red;color:bananas` becomes `color:bananas`). That's the same cause as #1392 and will be tracked there.
